description: The plot illustrates the sparsity ratio of SDPA (Scaled Dot-Product Attention) output across different layers of a model, with a threshold of $1 \times 10^{-2}$. The x-axis represents the layer number, ranging from 0 to 22, while the y-axis shows the sparsity ratio, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0. Three distinct lines are plotted: a blue dashed line labeled "sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.03" shows a low and relatively stable sparsity ratio across all layers, remaining near 0.01–0.02. An orange dotted line labeled "sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.44" starts at a high sparsity ratio (around 0.98) at layer 0 and declines sharply to approximately 0.4 by layer 10, then fluctuates between 0.2 and 0.4 for the remaining layers. A green solid line labeled "sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.33" begins at a sparsity ratio of about 0.98 at layer 0, decreases rapidly to around 0.2 by layer 10, and then stabilizes at a lower level, fluctuating between 0.05 and 0.15 for deeper layers. The legend indicates that the average sparsity ratios for the respective lines are 0.03, 0.44, and 0.33. This visualization highlights the effect of gating mechanisms on the sparsity of attention outputs, with the "after gate" line showing a higher average sparsity compared to the "before gate" and "after average gate" lines.
